items.prompt: Which sentence is in the passive voice?

options.text: The ball broke the window.
options.why: The ball does the action, so this is active.

options.text: The window is big.
options.why: This describes the window. No action is done to it.

options.text: The window was broken by the ball.
The children are playing ball.
options.why: The children do the action, so this is active.

hints: In a passive sentence, the subject has the action done to it.
Passive sentences use a form of be with a past participle, such as was broken.
Find the sentence where the window has something done to it.
items.explanation: In The window was broken by the ball, the window receives the action. Was broken is a passive verb.

items.prompt: Sort the sentences into active and passive.

items.text: The rice was cooked by the chef.
The letter was posted on Monday.

hints: Ask who or what is doing the action in each sentence.
In an active sentence, the subject does the action. In a passive one, the subject receives it.
Look for was or were followed by a verb ending in -ed.
items.explanation: In active sentences the subject does the action, as in The chef cooked the rice. In passive sentences the subject receives the action, as in The rice was cooked.

items.prompt: Complete the passive sentence in the past tense. Yesterday, the cake ___ eaten by the children.
hints: A passive verb is made with a form of be and a past participle.
The cake is one thing, and the sentence is about yesterday.
The cake is one thing. Which past form of be goes with one thing: was or were?
items.explanation: Was eaten is the past passive. The cake received the action, and the children did it.

items.prompt: Lightning struck the old tree. Which sentence says this in the passive voice?

options.text: The old tree struck lightning.
options.why: This changes the meaning: now the tree does the striking.

options.text: The old tree was struck by lightning.
Lightning was struck by the old tree.
options.why: This changes who did the action.

options.text: The old tree is striking lightning.
options.why: This is active and changes the meaning.

hints: In the passive, the object of the active sentence becomes the subject.
What was struck? Start the new sentence with that.
Then use was with the past participle of strike.
items.explanation: The tree received the action, so it becomes the subject: The old tree was struck by lightning.

items.prompt: Rewrite the sentence in the active voice. The poster was designed by Laila. Laila ___ the poster.
hints: In the active voice, the person who does the action comes first.
Laila did the designing.
Use the simple past tense of design.
items.explanation: In the active sentence, Laila does the action: Laila designed the poster.

items.prompt: Read: The water was heated to 50 °C. Why do science reports often use the passive voice like this?

options.text: It puts the focus on what was done, which matters more than who did it.
It makes the sentence funnier.
options.why: Science reports are not meant to be funny.

options.text: It shows that the experiment will happen in the future.
It is the only correct way to write about water.
options.why: Active sentences about water are also correct.

hints: Think about what matters most in an experiment.
In a passive sentence, the person doing the action can be left out.
Ask: does it matter who heated the water?
items.explanation: Science reports focus on the method and results. The passive voice keeps attention on what was done, not on the person who did it.

items.prompt: Which passive sentence is used because we do not know who did the action?

options.text: The school gate was left open last night.
The match was won by our team.
options.why: We know who won: our team.

options.text: The song was sung by Dina.
options.why: We know who sang it: Dina.

options.text: The picture was painted by my aunt.

hints: Look for a passive sentence without by and a person.
If the sentence names who did it, we know the person.
Find the sentence where the doer is a mystery.
items.explanation: Nobody knows who left the gate open, so the passive voice lets the writer leave out the doer.

items.prompt: Match each active sentence to the passive sentence with the same meaning.
pairs: The cat was chased by the dog.
The dog was chased by the cat.
The cat is chasing the dog.
The dog is being chased by the cat.
The dog will chase the cat.
The cat will be chased by the dog.
hints: Read each sentence very carefully. They look alike.
Check who is chasing and who is being chased, then check the tense.
Start with The dog chased the cat. Who received the action?
items.explanation: In the passive, the one being chased becomes the subject, and the tense must stay the same: chased, is chasing and will chase each have their own passive form.

items.prompt: Change the sentence into the passive without saying who did it. Someone has eaten all the biscuits. All the biscuits ___.
hints: The biscuits become the subject of the new sentence.
Keep the same tense as has eaten, and leave out someone.
Biscuits are plural. Which form of have goes with a plural subject?
items.explanation: Has eaten becomes have been eaten in the passive, because biscuits is plural: All the biscuits have been eaten.

items.prompt: Which sentence is not in the passive voice?

options.text: The bridge was being repaired.
options.why: This is passive: was being repaired.

options.text: The winners have been announced.
options.why: This is passive: have been announced.

options.text: The parcel had arrived early.
The plants are watered every day.

hints: A passive verb always has a form of be with a past participle.
Look for is, are, was, were, been or being in each sentence.
Check the sentence with had. Is there a form of be?
items.explanation: The parcel had arrived early is active: the parcel did the arriving. Had arrived is the past perfect, and there is no form of be.
